Episodes 1 to 6 of 18 are authored: 307 entities, 2,208 exact mentions in original-en and 2,211 in modern-en, 306 of the 307 bound in the older edition and 304 in the modern one, 59 focused tests passing, content revision 2026-09-14.6. NEXT: episode 7 (Aeolus, 539 paragraphs), the newspaper office -- headlined sections, and the first episode where Stephen and Bloom are in the same room. 5,746 paragraphs remain; the long ones are 15 (Circe, 1,441), 17 (Ithaca, 654), 11 (Sirens, 635), 12 (566) and 10 (546); episode 18 (Penelope) is eight paragraphs of monologue and will be the densest in the book.

THE TURN EPISODE 6 MAKES, AND THE ONE A LATER PASS IS MOST LIKELY TO BREAK: THE SURNAME DEDALUS CHANGES HANDS. Episodes 1 and 2 key 'Dedalus' and 'Mr Dedalus' to STEPHEN; FROM EPISODE 6 EVERY ONE OF THEM IS HIS FATHER SIMON, who sits in the funeral carriage all morning. The two tables are merged, keyed paragraph by paragraph, with no default, and a test asserts the rule (chapters 1-2 -> stephen, chapter 6 -> simon-dedalus). STEPHEN IS IN EPISODE 6 AND IS NEVER NAMED IN IT: he is 'a lithe young man, clad in mourning' seen once from the carriage, and 'your son and heir'. Both are phrase-bound.

A SURNAME IN THIS BOOK IS ALMOST NEVER ONE MAN, SO KEY BY DEFAULT AND ALIAS ONLY ON PROOF. There is no bare 'Bloom' default and 4:38 -- SLIEVE BLOOM, the mountains in Offaly -- is deliberately not keyed. Episode 6 added the sharpest namesake case yet: TWO O'CONNELLS, and one paragraph that holds both. 6:330 names John O'Connell the caretaker and, four lines later, Daniel O'Connell; it is keyed by occurrence. THE ADJACENCY SWEEP IS WHAT CAUGHT IT -- it was binding both to the caretaker. TWEEDY is three people: Molly's father, the crown solicitor for Waterford at 6:103, and Molly herself at 6:305. FRIDAY at 6:337 is Crusoe's Friday and then the day of the week, in one sentence.

THE THIRTEENTH MOURNER GETS HIS NAME FROM A MISTAKE: Bloom says 'macintosh', meaning the coat; Hynes writes M'INTOSH in his notebook as a name, and that is what the book calls him for the rest of its length. Both spans carry one card.

A SILENT BINDER LIMITATION THAT APPLIES TO EVERY BOOK IN THIS LIBRARY: reviewed_aliases.py guards alias matches with \w, AND AN UNDERSCORE SATISFIES \w, so an alias whose occurrence sits inside Gutenberg italics (_like this_) BINDS NOTHING AND NOTHING REPORTS IT. Three cases so far, all keyed now: '_Los Demiurgos_' 3:1, '_Matcham's Masterstroke_' 4:162, '_That's not Mulcahy_' 6:325. Two of the three were found by the EDITION-ASYMMETRY CENSUS, because the modern edition has no italics -- run that census on every episode. test_no_alias_in_this_package_is_hidden_by_italics is the standing check; over all 18 episodes it still reports STEPHEN at 15:1133 (a stage direction) and PATRICE at 16:212, which is NOT Patrice Egan but 'the faubourg Saint Patrice'.

THE MODERN EDITION IS A REWRITE AND CHANGES THE CAST OF A PARAGRAPH IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. It DELETES names (Chrysostomos 1:9, Mercury 1:293, Loyola 1:101, Adam Findlater and Dan Tallon 4:37, Hanlon 4:13, Wren 6:204) and SUPPLIES names Joyce did not write (Aristotle 3:0, Brian Boru 3:57, Deasy 3:10, Queen Victoria 3:94, M'Coy 5:27, Daniel O'Connell 6:106/6:277/6:278, Madame Bloom 6:104, Shakespeare 6:333, Martha 6:386). Two entities are reachable in one edition only: BRIAN BORU in the modern alone, ADAM FINDLATER in the older alone. No edition byte was touched. This lane never sets appStatus.
